target_customer: Texas homes and small businesses buying retail electricity, especially those wanting renewable plans
problem: Texas retail electricity plans carry middleman costs, and green plans are usually priced at a premium. GEX aimed to sell renewable power directly at lower prices.
business_model: licensed retail electric provider selling renewable electricity plans in ERCOT, margin on retail supply

founders.name: Patrick Woodson
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists him as the only founder and gives no background. Later news items call him CEO of a Texas power marketer.

exit.reason: No shutdown or sale announcement found; the YC directory marks the company Inactive and CB Insights marks it Dead.

competitors.name: Green Mountain Energy
competitors.what: Established Texas retail provider of renewable electricity plans
competitors.traction_then: incumbent brand in the Texas retail market
competitors.funding_then: owned by NRG, not independently funded

technical_complexity.rationale: A retail electric provider mainly needs ERCOT registration, wholesale supply and billing software. The hard parts are licensing and credit support, not novel technology.

defensibility.rationale: Any licensed retailer can sell renewable plans and customers compare plans on price. The REP license is a barrier to entry but did not differentiate GEX from dozens of rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent retailers already sold green plans and launched more in 2019; no source shows any of them acting against GEX specifically.

market_need_then: Texas has a deregulated retail market with many providers, and renewable plan demand was growing; a price-led green plan answered a stated customer complaint about green premiums.

branding.domain_note: Used getgex.com, a non-exact abbreviation domain; it now redirects to a domain sale page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Price and mission language: cutting out middlemen to increase clean energy adoption (from the YC description).

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand, no logo or community evidence found, and the GEX abbreviation is easily confused with the larger Gexa Energy brand.

outcome_analysis: GEX entered a crowded deregulated Texas retail market with a three person team, a $150K YC investment and a Shell credit facility in 2020. The cause of its inactivity is not public. The factors listed are inferred only from the market structure: many incumbent retailers selling green plans, and no differentiation beyond price. The 2021 Texas retailer failures after winter storm Uri are a plausible stress but no source ties them to GEX.
notes: Seed round and the $2.0M valuation rest on databases (CB Insights, TechLeap); Seedtable shows no rounds. The Shell Energy credit facility of May 2020 is known from search result summaries of a press release that could not be opened (fetch failed), so the amount is unknown. The failure factors are low confidence because the cause is not public. Company website now redirects to a domain broker page.
